speaker: Unknown
en: SpaceX, at least when I was there, the product was getting things to orbit.
zh: SpaceX,至少在我待的时候，产品是把东西送上轨道。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was not building an incredible software platform.
zh: 而不是打造一个了不起的软件平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we did build actually went viral internally at SpaceX.
zh: 我们实际做出来的东西在 SpaceX 内部确实走红了一阵。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talked to a number of other companies out there and asked like, what are you guys using?
zh: 我和外面不少公司聊过，问他们，你们在用什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you guys doing?
zh: 你们在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were like, oh man, it's awful.
zh: 他们说，哦天哪，糟透了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was just thinking about the future.
zh: 我当时只是在思考未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the most impact that I could have?
zh: 我能产生最大的影响是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that at SpaceX or is it leaving SpaceX and delivering this type of platform for all the other companies out there trying to build incredible machines?
zh: 是留在 SpaceX,还是离开 SpaceX,把这种平台交付给外面所有那些正在尝试打造了不起的机器的公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, Rebel provides a software platform for controlling hardware systems like nuclear reactors, jet engine test facilities, systems like oil and gas refineries.
zh: 今天，Rebel 为控制硬件系统提供软件平台，比如核反应堆、喷气发动机测试设施、石油和天然气炼油厂之类的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the biggest keys to SpaceX's success is just that Elon is willing to make massive bets on his team, even though everyone's like, we have no idea how this is going to work.
zh: SpaceX 成功的最大关键之一就是，Elon 愿意在他的团队身上下巨大的赌注，即使所有人都说，我们完全不知道这东西会怎么运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started building the catch tower before Starship had ever flown.
zh: 我们在 Starship 还从未飞过之前就开始建造接住塔了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone at SpaceX was like, this is crazy.
zh: SpaceX 的每个人都说，这太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, it was caught on Flight 5.
zh: 而最终，它在第 5 次飞行中被接住了。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the best parts of being at Revel is that in one day you can go to a nuclear reactor company, you can go to the most cutting edge satellite manufacturer, and then you can go to like a hypercar company.
zh: 在 Revel 最好的一点是，一天之内你可以去一家核反应堆公司，可以去最前沿的卫星制造商，然后还可以去一家超跑公司之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty cool.
zh: 挺酷的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Modern AI systems have made software easier than ever to build, cooling venture capital investment in the category and hammering public software stocks.
zh: 现代 AI 系统让软件的构建变得前所未有地容易，这给该品类的风险投资降温，并重挫了公开市场的软件股。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what makes Revel one of 2026's narrative violations, a software startup thriving amid the chill.
zh: 这正是 Revel 成为 2026 年叙事违背者的原因之一——一家在寒潮中蓬勃发展的软件初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Founded in 2024 by SpaceX veteran Scott Morton,
zh: 它由 SpaceX 老兵 Scott Morton 于 2024 年创立，

speaker: Unknown
en: Revel makes testing and control software for companies building rockets, supersonic aircraft, nuclear reactors, and other complex machines.
zh: Revel 为那些制造火箭、超音速飞机、核反应堆和其他复杂机器的公司制作测试与控制软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: In less than two years, it's raised $180 million, won customers like Impulse Space and Radiant Nuclear, and was reportedly valued at just over $1 billion.
zh: 在不到两年时间里，它融资了 1.8 亿美元，赢得了 Impulse Space 和 Radiant Nuclear 这样的客户，据报道估值刚超过 10 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: In today's episode, Scott and I discuss the hardware renaissance, why industrial software got stuck in the 1980s,
zh: 在今天的节目中，Scott 和我讨论硬件复兴、为什么工业软件卡在了 20 世纪 80 年代，

speaker: Unknown
en: What he learned from Elon Musk and why Revel decided to create its own programming language.
zh: 他从 Elon Musk 那里学到了什么，以及为什么 Revel 决定创造自己的编程语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Mario and this is The Generalist.
zh: 我是 Mario,这是 The Generalist。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great to have you here.
zh: 很高兴你来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited to chat and learn more about you and Revel.
zh: 我非常期待和你聊天，更多了解你和 Revel。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one of the interesting places to start is maybe noting the sense of Revel being almost a little bit of a narrative violation.
zh: 我觉得一个有趣的切入点，也许是指出 Revel 在某种程度上几乎算是一个叙事违背者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We live in a world in which the dominant narrative is that AI is sort of solving all software.
zh: 我们生活在这样一个世界里，主流叙事是 AI 正在某种意义上解决所有软件问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that every company will sort of maybe build their own systems entirely from scratch.
zh: 而且每家公司也许都会完全从零开始构建自己的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you are building a software company for the most demanding buyers in many ways in the world.
zh: 而你正在为世界上许多方面要求最高的买家打造一家软件公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where's the disconnect that people miss in that narrative that leaves the space for Revel to thrive in the way that you have?
zh: 在那个叙事中，人们遗漏了什么脱节点，才给 Revel 留下了像你这样蓬勃发展的空间？

speaker: Unknown
en: The biggest thing is...
zh: 最重要的一点是……

speaker: Unknown
en: That I don't think anyone's really going to kind of bet their career on like vibe coding a control system for let's say a nuclear reactor or a rocket engine or something that's very high consequence.
zh: 我不认为真的有人会把自己的职业生涯押在，比如说，用 vibe coding 写一个核反应堆或火箭引擎或某种后果非常严重的系统的控制系统上。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of these I think kind of shallow web apps that are very easy to code I think definitely I think those are maybe in trouble with the new capabilities of AI but
zh: 我认为很多这类很容易编写的浅层 web 应用，我觉得它们在新一代 AI 能力面前肯定可能有麻烦，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, fundamentally, a company is like an asymmetric capability.
zh: 我觉得，从根本上说，一家公司就像一种不对称能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a group of people that are really specialized in this space.
zh: 你有一群在这个领域里真正专业化的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at Revel, I mean, we are fully leveraging AI tools as much as we possibly can.
zh: 而在 Revel,我是说，我们在尽可能充分地利用 AI 工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there is a lot more that goes into software that controls these high-stakes systems than just authoring code.
zh: 但是，控制这些高风险系统的软件，需要做的远不止编写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a full CI system.
zh: 我们有一套完整的 CI 系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what that is is like...
zh: 它是这样的……

speaker: Unknown
en: A bunch of hardware that we control is in a lab.
zh: 我们控制的一堆硬件放在一个实验室里。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have every type of hardware or kind of system that our platform supports.
zh: 我们的每一种平台支持的硬件或系统，我们都有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And anytime we do a release, it goes through a whole process that takes several days to make sure that it is all correct.
zh: 每次我们做发布，它都要经过一个耗时数天的完整流程，以确保一切都是正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we release it to our customers, it's going to behave as we expect.
zh: 这样当我们把它发布给客户时，它会按我们预期的方式运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, vibe coding only really helps with the authorship component.
zh: 另外，vibe coding 真正有帮助的只是编写这个环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with our stack, everything, every line of code is reviewed by someone that you have the right person at the company to review it.
zh: 所以在我们的技术栈里，每一行代码都由某人审查，确保公司里有合适的人来审查它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've seen a lot of, I mean, internally, we've seen a lot of kind of acceleration of our authorship, but not necessarily, but there's a lot more that goes into releasing correct software to control physical systems.
zh: 所以我们看到了很多，我是说，在内部，我们看到了编写环节的很多加速，但不一定……但是，发布能控制物理系统的正确软件，还有更多环节要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a version of the future where you think, hey, if these models get so good at this trajectory, maybe there's something we have to do very differently?
zh: 有没有一种可能的未来版本，你会想，嘿，如果这些模型在这条轨迹上变得这么好，也许有什么事情我们必须以非常不同的方式去做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or will it always just be the case that, hey, yes, those models can keep getting better.
zh: 还是说情况永远都会是，嘿，是的，那些模型可以不断变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That'll just help us deliver an increasingly better system.
zh: 那只会帮助我们交付一个越来越好的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so far what we're seeing, it's only just enabling us to move a lot faster.
zh: 我想到目前为止我们所看到的，它只是让我们能够快很多地推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then again, we have the kind of specialization in the area.
zh: 而且再说一次，我们有这个领域里的专业化分工。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we have people, we're a pretty tenured group so far, actually.
zh: 比如我们的人，实际上到目前为止我们是一个资历相当深的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're pretty light on junior engineers.
zh: 我们初级工程师相当少。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do want to hire more junior engineers in the next few months, but...
zh: 我们确实想在未来几个月里多招一些初级工程师，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of mostly kind of former SpaceX senior engineers.
zh: 团队大概主要是前 SpaceX 的高级工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have several from Palantir and Andrel as well.
zh: 我们也有几位来自 Palantir 和 Andrel 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But arming these people with AI where they really know what they're doing, they know what the correct solution really looks like just kind of through their experience has been a huge accelerant for us.
zh: 但是给这些人装备上 AI——他们真正知道自己在做什么，他们通过自己的经验真正知道正确的解决方案长什么样——这对我们来说是一个巨大的加速器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it'll kind of continue in that direction.
zh: 而且我认为这个方向还会继续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it's part of the reason I was excited to have this conversation is that I think Revel feels like an example of what an amazing next-gen software company could look like that you don't want to outsource this capability in.
zh: 是的，我觉得这也是我兴奋地进行这次对话的部分原因，因为我认为 Revel 感觉上像是一个惊人的下一代软件公司可能是什么样子的例子——那种你不会想把这种能力外包出去的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe to take another beat and give folks a better sense of what it is exactly that Revel does, can you sort of give folks a little bit of the texture there?
zh: 也许可以再换个节拍，让大家更清楚地了解 Revel 到底是做什么的，你能不能给大家讲一讲这方面的具体情况？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so RIVL provides a software platform for controlling hardware systems.
zh: 是的，RIVL 提供一个用于控制硬件系统的软件平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hardware systems being like nuclear reactors.
zh: 硬件系统比如核反应堆。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do rocket engine test sites, jet engine test facilities, and then also kind of industrial scale systems like oil and gas refineries.
zh: 我们做火箭发动机试验场、喷气发动机试验设施，还有工业规模的系统，比如石油和天然气炼油厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's really exciting right now is we're kind of moving more in that direction.
zh: 而现在真正令人兴奋的是，我们正在更多地朝那个方向推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fundamental problem that we're solving is that the software in this space really hasn't made any kind of material improvements since the 1980s and 90s.
zh: 而我们正在解决的根本问题是，这个领域的软件自 1980 年代和 90 年代以来真的没有任何实质性的改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw this problem firsthand at SpaceX.
zh: 我在 SpaceX 亲眼见过这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: To have something great at SpaceX, we had to build it all ourselves.
zh: 在 SpaceX 要做出好东西，我们只能全都自己造。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was part of the team that did that.
zh: 而我就是做这件事的团队的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I was just thinking about the future and like, what is the most impact that I could have in the space?
zh: 后来我一直在思考未来，比如，我能在这个领域产生的最大影响是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that at SpaceX or is it...
zh: 是留在 SpaceX，还是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Leaving SpaceX and delivering this type of platform for all the other companies out there trying to build incredible machines.
zh: 离开 SpaceX，为所有其他正在尝试制造了不起的机器的公司交付这种类型的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard you mention that, you know, the fact that this sort of state of play has been stuck in the 80s and 90s before.
zh: 我听你之前提到过，这种现状一直卡在 80 年代和 90 年代的事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, why do you think that's been the case?
zh: 比如，你为什么会认为是这样？

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you think about what's been stuck, has it been truly the underlying capabilities that are stuck there?
zh: 还有，当你思考到底是什么被卡住了，是底层能力真的卡在那里了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it more just the interface layer that is, you know, incredibly web 1.0 and just not what people are used to in terms of polish?
zh: 还是更多只是界面层，你知道的，极其 web 1.0，完全不是人们在精致度上所习惯的样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it both of those things?
zh: 是两者都有吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think just all the software engineering talent got very excited about the internet technologies.
zh: 我觉得只是所有的软件工程人才都对互联网技术变得非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can really just see it.
zh: 你真的可以看出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like these tools that are available really do date back.
zh: 就像这些可用的工具真的可以追溯到很早。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like 1986 is when one of the major platforms used in tests was invented and really hasn't changed much since then.
zh: 比如 1986 年是测试中使用的一个主要平台被发明的时间，而且从那以后真的没怎么变过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then 1993 is when the platform that's generally used in industrials was created.
zh: 然后 1993 年是工业界普遍使用的那个平台被创造出来的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can see then 1998 nothing and then all the way through 2000s.
zh: 然后你可以看到 1998 年什么都没有，然后一直贯穿到 2000 年代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's really just all the software engineering talent went and worked on the internet.
zh: 而我觉得真的就是所有的软件工程人才都跑去从事互联网了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this space just kind of languished.
zh: 而这个领域就这样被荒废了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There weren't really any startups focused on this.
zh: 真的没有什么初创公司专注于这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was no real pressure on the incumbents to really innovate.
zh: 在位者身上没有任何真正的创新压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think then companies like SpaceX came along and proved that you could do interesting things in hardware.
zh: 所以我觉得后来像 SpaceX 这样的公司出现了，证明了你可以在硬件上做出有意思的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, you know, there's definitely Revel is kind of part of a couple of companies now that are really focused on this.
zh: 而我觉得，你知道，Revel 显然是现在真正专注于这个的几家公司之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And presumably it's also just a testament to how sticky these solutions are that once they're ingrained, it's very hard to rip them out such that you mentioned there haven't been many startups in the space.
zh: 而且大概这也证明了这些解决方案的粘性有多强——一旦它们根深蒂固，就很难把它们拔除，以至于你提到这个领域没有很多初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But looking over the last five, 10 years, I've seen a few folks try and take a chip at it.
zh: 但回顾过去五到十年，我见过一些人尝试过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels really hard for folks to make the sort of progress that you guys actually have done.
zh: 而感觉上人们很难取得你们实际做到的那种进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's that disconnect there?
zh: 那个脱节在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I had this question.
zh: 是的，我有这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, could Revel have been invented any time in the last decade?
zh: 另外，Revel 有可能在过去十年里的任何时候被发明出来吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, what's different?
zh: 是的，有什么不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it could have.
zh: 我觉得它本来是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really do.
zh: 我真的这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, I think a lot of the companies that are in our space are similar in that they are actually looking to what SpaceX did.
zh: 而且，我觉得我们这个领域里很多公司都很相似，它们实际上都在看 SpaceX 做过的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're kind of modeling.
zh: 它们都在某种程度上以它为榜样。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this lighthouse flying light.
zh: 有一座灯塔在发光。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think SpaceX really is.
zh: 而 SpaceX 确实就是。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the ultimate proving ground for software, for hardware.
zh: 它就像是软件、硬件的终极试验场。

speaker: Unknown
en: They try to move as fast as they possibly can.
zh: 他们尽可能地快速行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will make big investments to move really quickly.
zh: 他们会进行大规模投资来真正快速地推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was fortunate to write a ton of control software at SpaceX and then also work on, how are we going to do this in the future?
zh: 我很幸运在 SpaceX 写了大量的控制软件，然后还参与了，我们未来要怎么做这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think there was just a kind of accumulation of a lot of experience.
zh: 所以我觉得这是大量经验的积累。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it's that experience what we were taking forward to Revel.
zh: 然后正是这些经验，我们把它带到了 Revel。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of, it's pretty simple.
zh: 这有点，挺简单的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to have this kind of incubator to figure out what the next generation of systems look like.
zh: 你需要有这样一个孵化器，来弄清楚下一代系统是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then those people can then go and take that experience outside the company.
zh: 然后这些人就可以带着这些经验走出公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if I have to synthesize it a little bit, it feels like the old set of software didn't develop because there was this massive talent problem where everyone just moves to the internet.
zh: 所以如果让我稍微总结一下，感觉旧的那套软件之所以没有发展，是因为存在一个巨大的人才问题，所有人都流向了互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plus, it's super sticky, so there's not an incentive to rip it out.
zh: 再加上它黏性极强，所以没有动力把它拆掉换新。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then the few newcomers that come in don't have this experience where they get to see exactly how to build this from the inside of somewhere like SpaceX and learn, okay, here are all these edge cases and it's tough to get these companies to adopt it unless it's perfect anyway.
zh: 然后少数进来的新玩家，又没有这种经验——能在 SpaceX 这样的地方从内部亲眼看到如何构建这套系统，学到，好，这里有这么多边缘情况，而且除非做到完美，否则很难让这些公司采用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You kind of have a bit of a chicken and egg issue there.
zh: 那里你多少会有一个先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that sort of a decent distillation of some of the dynamics that Revel was walking into?
zh: 这算是对 Revel 当初所面对的这些动态的一个还算不错的提炼吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I would add also that SpaceX is this pressure cooker.
zh: 是的，我还想补充一点，SpaceX 是一个高压锅。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were extremely motivated to think very hard about this.
zh: 而我们非常有动力去认真深入地思考这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we had Elon's backing to go and try a few things.
zh: 然后我们有 Elon 的支持，可以去尝试一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also had accumulated decades of experience elsewhere inside the company.
zh: 我们还在公司内部其他地方积累了数十年的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: The system has to work.
zh: 系统必须能工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has to also have evidence that it's accelerating the team.
zh: 它还必须有证据表明它在加速团队的进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the combination of those things is what kind of results in greatness.
zh: 我觉得这些东西的组合，才造就了卓越。
